title: Gov. Hochul expands NY free community college to address AI workforce impacts
source_used: New York Daily News (fulltext/C14-11.txt, 2,328 chars, HTTP 200)
key_facts: New York's free community college initiative is expanding to tens of thousands more adult learners to help address the impact of AI on the workforce, Governor Hochul said on Monday 5 Oct 2026.

Starting in January, CUNY and SUNY students aged 25 to 55 can enrol tuition-free in select 'high-demand' associate degree programmes regardless of their background in higher education; previously the initiative was only for adults without a college degree.
The governor framed the expansion as one strategy to help New Yorkers in jobs vulnerable to automation switch careers without paying for more schooling.
More than 15,000 students have enrolled in free community college degree programmes, such as advanced manufacturing and cybersecurity, since the initiative launched in 2025.
Applications open before the spring semester, with enrolment periods varying across dozens of SUNY and CUNY campuses.
SUNY Chancellor John King Jr. and CUNY Chancellor Felix Matos Rodriguez backed the expansion in statements.
Hochul has already announced an AI-focused commission to propose policies by the end of the year on career training and placement and on strengthening the social safety net.

The New York City Council is considering AI legislation including whistleblower protection and a kill-switch requirement; representatives of Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta were set to testify on Monday.

why_it_matters_hint: Adults whose jobs AI may change get a tuition-free route to retrain, though the article does not show how many jobs AI is displacing in New York.
event_date: Announced Monday 5 Oct 2026; takes effect January 2027.
